text:
vikram: quick thread — thinking about long-term approach for multi-dc active/active with strict data residency for EMEA customers. do we bind tenant -> DC or do soft-pin + request routing? need tradeoffs.
jess: For privacy, strong bind (tenant pinned) is simplest. But it reduces capacity elasticity across regions.
anna: soft-pin + origin header works if we can guarantee no cross-region KV replication for pinned tenants.
miles: main pain: session cache and KV lease handoffs. current lease-swap is eventual; could leak data during failover.
vikram: idea: introduce "jurisdiction tag" on tenant namespace and enforce no replication of namespace across non-consent regions. that means local-only KV + async archive to compliant storage.
jess: downside: if local DC fails we must fail open to other DC or block requests. compliance may forbid failover. have we seen customers require hard block?
anna: legal said some require hard block (no processing outside EU). So we need configurable policies per tenant: ["hard_block", "soft_pin", "replicate_with_masking"].
miles: operationally, hard_block => reduce SLA significantly. can we implement transparent degrade mode returning 503 with clear error code?
vikram: yes. proposal sketch:
```
tenant_policy:
  id: <tenant id>
  jurisdiction: eu
  failover_policy: hard_block|soft_pin|allow_failover_masked
  kv_replication: disabled|encrypted_archive
```
anna: also add "allowed_failover_zones" list for customers that want limited cross-region fallback (e.g., within EU only).
sre-bot: FYI: incident runbook update required if hard_block tenants scale to >10% of traffic.
miles: tech tradeoff: implementing hard_block cheap in router (deny route), hard in stateful services (must ensure no side-effect writes to shared metrics, backups).
jess: another angle: use edge-proxy to do initial residency check and reject before hitting backend. cheaper.
vikram: agree. edge check + tenant_policy store in primary DC. router consults cached policy with TTL 30s.
infra-bot: perf test note: adding policy lookup adds 0.8ms p95 on our canary; consider local cache per worker.
anna: next steps: 1) update policy schema (RFC draft), 2) prototype edge-check + cache, 3) tabletop for failover scenarios. assign owners?
vikram: i'll draft RFC. @anna can you prototype edge-check? @miles update runbook snippets?
anna: yep, I'll pick it up. quick question — do we version tenant policy schema? need migration plan.
miles: yes start with v1 with default soft_pin for existing tenants.
jess: +1. also add telemetry events: residency_blocked, residency_failed_over.
vikram: thanks all. keeping this thread for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
